findings.title: [P1] Restore listener detachment in `unmount()`
findings.body: `mount()` now registers an anonymous closure via `socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))` without storing it, and `unmount()` was reduced to `this.socket = undefined`, dropping the previous `this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)` call. Consequences under realistic usage: (1) after any `mount()` → `unmount()` cycle, a live socket still holds the listener, so every subsequent `"message"` event calls `render()` on the torn-down view; (2) each closure retains the `SocketView`, so the socket leaks the view's memory; (3) remounting accumulates duplicate listeners — with a reused socket each message renders once per prior mount, and a stale socket can drive a newly remounted view. Since the handler reference is gone, the only fix is to restore the stored reference (`this.onMessage`) and the `off` call before clearing `this.socket`. Verified against the diff hunks and the full file; no other file, caller, or test removes the listener.
